question.text: The SIA is debriefing the board of Bal Vikas Samiti on how 80G status affects donor inflow via the NSE-SSE ZCZP e-IPO platform. Which of the following is TRUE about the e-IPO 80G facility described in the chapter?

answer.text: Donors can contribute from INR 10,000 via registered brokers (SCSB / Syndicate Members with 3-in-1 accounts) and can avail 80G benefits
The minimum contribution via the e-IPO is INR 50,000; 80G is NOT available for e-IPO donations
80G is available only if the donation is made in physical cash at the NPO's office
The e-IPO platform only supports corporate CSR donors, not individuals

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p.215 of the workbook, NSE-SSE has introduced a facility for bidding of ZCZP instruments on the e-IPO platform for Self-Certified Syndicate Banks (SCSBs) and Syndicate Members with 3-in-1 accounts. Donors can contribute from INR 10,000 through their registered brokers and avail 80G benefits. Per p.216, cash donations above INR 2,000 are ineligible for 80G deduction. The Trap: The minimum is INR 10,000, not INR 50,000, and 80G is supported for e-IPO inflows. Cash donations above INR 2,000 do not qualify for 80G. The e-IPO is not restricted to corporate CSR donors. Note: Pair the p.215 e-IPO facts with the p.216 INR 2,000 cash-donation cap when explaining donor-side 80G eligibility.
